title: Will Asteroid Mining Affect Global Equity?

limitations: Indicator table layout is misaligned in text extraction.

tasks: Task 1: Define global equity and build measurement model
Task 2: Describe future asteroid mining and its equity impact
Task 3: Analyze impact under changing conditions
Task 4: Policy recommendations for updating the Outer Space Treaty

section_map.summary: Four-task abstract: TOPSIS equity, cluster mining vision, comparative advantage, UN policy
Background on resource depletion, Outer Space Treaty, four tasks
4+21 indicator system, EWM+CV weights, TOPSIS, 32 countries
Lambda perturbation on four countries, stable
Five strengths, three weaknesses, three improvements

contributions.summary: EWM + coefficient of variation combined weighting avoids AHP subjectivity and equalization.
Eight-sector asteroid mining chain derived from upstream-midstream-downstream analysis.
Ricardo comparative advantage reallocation vs capability allocation.
Grey model forecast showing comparative advantage flattens the negative equity slope.

dependency_graph.handoff: TOPSIS closeness scores feed the sector clustering and equity comparison

assumptions.summary: Mineral types and technical differences ignored.
Selected indicators effectively reflect global equity.
Data from authoritative sources is accurate.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 21 indicators, 32 countries, from UN, WIPO, World Bank, World Energy Council. Missing values: same-class mean, mean/mode, MLE.

models.summary: GEI: TOPSIS with EWM+CV combined weights, 32 countries ranked.
SEC: K-means sector assignment, Ricardo reallocation, GM(1,1) forecast.

verification.summary: Lambda sensitivity on US, Japan, Brazil, Germany: only minor score changes.
Grey model level-ratio test passed before forecasting.

results_trace.summary: Germany 0.648 rank 1, Switzerland 0.645, Sweden 0.635, Morocco 0.406 rank 32.
Capability allocation: US dominates, gap widens, not conducive to equity.
Comparative advantage: negative impact shrinks over time.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract uses 'In order to...' repeated four times, one per task.
Definition built bottom-up: four aspects then 'To sum up' synthesis.
Proverb 'an able man is always busy' frames the capability allocation before critique.
Policy section quotes the Outer Space Treaty verbatim then reinterprets 'freedom'.

language_observations.summary: 'a conceivable and attempted task' — paired adjectives, one about possibility, one about action.
'deepen the situation of one superpower and many powers' — geopolitical idiom applied to equity.
'people are gradually seeing the light of day' — idiom for emerging feasibility.
Rejects AHP explicitly for 'strong subjectivity' — justifies method choice by naming the defect.
'an able man is always busy' — proverb opens the allocation discussion.
'Looking back at our original intentions' — self-referential pivot to change the model.
Quotes treaty text then argues it 'does not specifically explain the scope' — quote-then-critique pattern.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Explicit rejection of AHP subjectivity shows methodological self-awareness.
Importing Ricardo's comparative advantage into space mining is a creative cross-domain move.
Quote-then-critique of the Outer Space Treaty grounds policy in legal text.

weaknesses.summary: Indicator selection has room for improvement.
Transaction and exchange rate risks not considered.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Dual objective weighting (entropy + variation) avoids single-method defects.
Treaty-text reinterpretation gives policy legal grounding.

unresolved_questions.question: Why lambda = 0.5 exactly? No optimization shown.
How many clusters K were used, and how was K chosen?
